questions.question: You have configured a router with the following command. However, when you enter show ip routes you do not see any routes for OSPF. What is the problem? Router(config)#router ospf 255 Router(config-router)#network 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0 area 255
questions.explanation: The wildcard mask is incorrect because it is a bitmask, which is the opposite of a subnet mask. The 1s in the host section, rather than 1s in the network section, define the wildcard. The correct wildcard mask is 0.0.0.255 for this configuration.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which state in the neighbor table indicates that the router has successfully downloaded the LSA information from a neighboring router?
questions.explanation: The FULL state is only achieved after the router has created an adjacency with a neighbor router and downloaded the LSAs to form its topological database.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You have two links that enter the same OSPF router with the same bandwidth. You want to prefer one route over the other yet allow the second as a backup route. Which command would you use to achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command ip ospf cost 25 should be configured on the interface that will act as the backup route. This adjustment of cost will allow the router to prefer the other route first.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command will display the designated router for a LAN?
questions.explanation: The command show ip ospf interfaces will display the interface details of each interface for OSPF. In this information, the DR and BDR router ID will be displayed.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command will set the bandwidth of an interface to 2.048 Mb/s?
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is always specified in kilobits per second (Kb/s), so 2.048 Mb/s would be 2,048,000 bits per second, or 2,048 Kb/s.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see the networks the current router is advertising for OSPF?
questions.explanation: The command show ip protocols will list the router ID of the current router as well as the networks that are being advertised via OSPF on the current router.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which statement is true of routers in the same area?
choices: All routers in the same area have the same process IDs.
All routers in the same area have the same neighbor table.
All routers in the same area have the same topology table.
All routers in the same area have the same hello/dead timers.
questions.explanation: An area defines a topology inside of the OSPF hierarchy. Since each router in an area calculates its own costs, they all contain the same topological database, or LSDB.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command would you use to make sure Router A never becomes a designated router?
questions.explanation: All routers by default have an OSPF priority of 1. If you set the priority to 0, the router will never become a designated router. This command must be set in the interface.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You enter a show ip route command and see the following line. What does the [110/1] identify? O 192.168.3.0/24 [110/1] via 192.168.10.6, 00:58:55, Serial0/3/1
choices: Administrative distance of 110 and a 1 Gb/s link
Administrative distance of 1 and a 110 Mb/s link
Administrative distance of 110 and a 100 Mb/s link
Administrative distance of 110 and a 10 Mb/s link
questions.explanation: It identifies the administrative distance of 110 for OSPF. The cost calculation is the reference bandwidth of 100 Mb/s divided by the link bandwidth. This calculation would result in a cost of 1.
questions.topic: 3.9 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command will start an OSPFv3 process with an ID of 4?
questions.explanation: The command ipv6 router ospf 4 will start an IPv6 process with an ID of 4. Most IPv6 commands will start with ipv6 .
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which IPv6 address does OSPFv3 use to communicate with designated routers?
questions.explanation: OSPFv3 used the multicast address ff02::6 to send communications to designated routers.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: When configuring OSPFv3, how do you configure the router ID?
choices: The router ID is configured as the 64-bit host section of an IPv6 address.
The router ID is configured as a 32-bit IPv4 address.
The router ID is configured as a 128-bit IPv6 address.
The router ID is configured as a 48-bit MAC address.
questions.explanation: When an OSPFv3 process is configured, the process will handle IPv6. However, the router ID is still configured as an IPv4 address.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You are configuring an OSPFv3 process of 4 for an interface of Serial 0/0 with an IPv6 address of 2001:db8:1:2::1/64 in area 0. Which command will you use?
questions.explanation: With OSPFv3 IPv6 configuration, the duplication of long IPv6 network addresses can cause erroneous entries. So OSPFv3 is configured directly on the IPv6 link with the command ipv6 ospf 4 area 0 .
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You have an interface of Serial 0/0, which is connected to your ISP. You want to suppress OSPFv3 LSAs on the IPv6 link to the ISP. Which command will you use?
questions.explanation: Configuring OSPFv3 for a passive interface it is similar to configuring OSPFv2. However, the configuration prompt for IPv6 is Router(config-rtr)# .
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You have a number of routers with 10 Gb/s and 1 Gb/s links running OSPFv3. You need to adjust the cost for all links on the router. Which command will allow you to achieve this with the fewest commands?
questions.explanation: The easiest way to achieve this is to change the reference bandwidth from 100 Mb/s to 10 Gb/s. This is done as a command in the OSPFv3 router process with the command auto-cost reference- bandwidth 10000 . This will adjust the reference-bandwidth for all links associated with this process ID.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which IPv6 address does OSPFv3 use to send LSA hello packets?
questions.explanation: OSPFv3 used the multicast address ff02::5 to send hello packets to neighbor routers.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify only OSPFv3 routes?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 route ospf will display only the OSPFv3 routes.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which command would you use to verify that the hello/dead timers match for OSPFv3?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 ospf interface will display numerous stats about the interfaces participating in OSPFv3. One of the stats is the hello/dead timers.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: A common problem with IPv6 and OSPFv3 is MTU. Why is it a common problem with IPv6 and not IPv4?
choices: IPv6 addresses are large and require jumbo frames.
IPv4 uses TCP to transmit OSPF packets.
questions.explanation: IPv4 allows for packet fragmentation. However, IPv6 does not fragment packets because at the layer 3 header there is no fragmentation functionality. So close attention needs to be made to link MTUs on adjacent neighbors.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You need to configure OSPFv3 for the network 2001:db8:2:3/64 with an area of 0. Which configuration would you use?
questions.explanation: The configuration of OSPFv3 for IPv6 is always done on the interface. Area 0 can be represented as 0.0.0.0, because the area as defined by the RFC is a 32-bit value. The Cisco IOS allows you to enter the last octet of the area or the whole 32-bit value.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You begin to configure OSPFv3 but get the error % IPv6 routing not enabled. Which command needs to be entered?
questions.explanation: You must enable IPv6 routing via the command ipv6 unicast- routing in order to use OSPFv3.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You have configured OSPFv3 with a process ID of 5. You want to view only the OSPFv3 process ID of 5. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 ospf 5 will only show the OSPFv3 process ID of 5.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: You have two routers that will not form an OPSFv3 adjacency. You’ve identified that the hello timer on Router B has been changed. Which command will rectify the problem?
questions.explanation: The hello interval timer is configured per the interface, since broadcast (multi-access) would apply to a LAN interface vs. a non- broadcast multiple access (NBMA) network interface. The command no ipv6 ospf hello-interval will set the hello timer back to the original default value.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: After you configure a new router ID for an OSPFv3 process, which command must be entered for the change to take effect?
questions.explanation: The command to restart the OSPFv3 process is performed at the privileged exec command prompt. The command to be entered for OSPFv3 would be clear ipv6 ospf process . You will then be asked to confirm it.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: When configuring OSPFv3, what is an alternative to specifying a router ID?
choices: Specifying the command ipv6 ospf 1 area 0 on an IPv4 interface
Configuring the highest IP address on the network
questions.explanation: When you configure the command ipv6 ospf 1 area 0 on an IPv4 interface, the IP address on the interface is used as the router ID.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which statement is correct about OSPFv3 vs. OSPFv2?
choices: OSPFv3 will advertise all networks configured on a link.
OSPFv3 can load-balance links of unequal cost.
OSFPv3 requires directed broadcast enabled on the router.
OSPFv3 can run a maximum of four instances per router.
questions.explanation: Unlike OSPFv2, OSPFv3 will advertise all of the networks that are configured on a link in which OSPFv3 is configured. This replaces the need to use the network command, which is used in OSPFv2.
questions.topic: 3.10 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot single area and multi-area OSPFv3 for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub, virtuallink, and LSAs)

questions.question: Which dynamic routing protocol is a Cisco proprietary routing protocol?
questions.explanation: Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) is a Cisco proprietary dynamic routing protocol. Only Cisco routers can participate in EIGRP.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: By default, which metrics are used by EIGRP to calculate path cost?
questions.explanation: EIGRP can use bandwidth, delay, load, reliability, and MTU as the cost metrics. Default configuration of EIGRP only uses bandwidth and delay as the cost metrics, although others can be configured.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which is a requirement for EIGRP routers to create a neighborship?
questions.explanation: A requirement for routers to become neighbors is matching K metrics. The K metrics are values that can be adjusted for the EIGRP metrics of bandwidth, delay, load, reliability, and MTU.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which IPv4 multicast address is used by EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The Reliable Transport Protocol (RTP), which is part of EIGRP, uses 224.0.0.10 to send hello messages.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the default formula for metric calculation for EIGRP?
choices: metric = ([K1 * bandwidth + (K2 * bandwidth) / (256 – load) + K3 * delay] * [K5 / (reliability + K4)]) * 256
questions.explanation: The default metric calculation for EIGRP is metric = ((107 / least- bandwidth) + cumulative-delay) * 256.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which condition must be met for two routers participating in EIGRP to become neighbors?
questions.explanation: A neighbor requirement is matching autonomous system numbers. The autonomous system number is EIGRP’s scalability mechanism.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the default hop count of EIGRP?
questions.explanation: EIGRP has a default hop count of 100 hops before a packet is considered unroutable.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What mechanism does EIGRP have for scalability?
questions.explanation: EIGRP uses AS numbers to segment routing updates to an autonomous system. This provides scalability of the EIGRP routing protocol.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: How often are hello messages sent between EIGRP participating routers by default?
questions.explanation: The default hello timer for EIGRP is 5 seconds. This is performed by RTP.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: When does the EIGRP protocol advertise the entire database?
choices: When a route update is sent
questions.explanation: Upon forming an adjacency with its neighbor, EIGRP neighboring routers will send their entire database. After the initial load of the database, each router will watch for updates.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the maximum stable hop count for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The default hop count is 100 for EIGRP. However, the maximum stable hop count is 255 hops before a route is considered undeliverable.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which table is used to feed information to the topology table with EIGRP?
questions.explanation: Hello packets and the RTP table help to build the neighbor table. In return, the neighbor table sends this information to the topology table.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which mechanism does RTP use if an established neighbor does not respond to a multicast hello packet for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: If an established neighbor does not respond to its multicast hello packet, the router will send unicast packets. After 16 missed unicast packets, the neighbor will be declared dead. This process is called reliable multicast.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What happens when a hold interval for EIGRP has expired?
choices: The hello message is retransmitted via broadcast packets.
The hello message is retransmitted via unicast packets.
questions.explanation: When the hold interval has expired and a hello message has not been seen, the neighboring router is considered down or failed.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: How many equal-cost links can EIGRP load-balance?
questions.explanation: By default, EIGRP can load balance up to 4 equal-cost links.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which routing algorithm does EIGRP use?
questions.explanation: EIGRP uses the Diffusing Update Algorithm to calculate route cost.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: After a router has been acknowledged, which table is built from the network routes discovered for the EIGRP protocol?
questions.explanation: After the neighbor process has been established, the routers will exchange full topology tables with each other. These topology tables are sent in full, then maintained only by partial updates if a route changes.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: A router has learned two routes to the same network. EIGRP has a route to the destination network with a cost of 202342520. OSPF has a route to the destination network with a cost of 64. Which route will be used to the destination network?
choices: Both routes will be used with load balancing.
The routes will be used in a spill and fill configuration.
The EIGRP route with a cost of 202342520
The OSPF route with a cost of 64
questions.explanation: The cost of the link between routing protocols is irrelevant. The administrative distance (AD) of EIGRP is 90, and the AD of OSPF is 110. Therefore, the lowest AD routing protocol is used. If the EIGRP route becomes invalid or is removed from the routing table, then OSPF will be used.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the default hold interval for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The EIGRP hold interval by default is three times the hello interval. Since the hello interval is 5 seconds, the hold interval is 15 seconds. Hold intervals are usually three times the initial discovery interval.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which metric is considered to be infinite for an EIGRP route in which the router will not try to route packets to the destination network?
questions.explanation: EIGRP metrics are not based on hops. EIGRP metrics are based on bandwidth and delay as a composite metric. The metric can be a very large number, but the limit to this metric in which the route is considered invalid is 2 32 – 1.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which statement is correct about EIGRP and how it works with updates?
choices: EIGRP sends changes to routes only when they are detected.
EIGRP sends its full routing table during each hello interval.
EIGRP sends its link state during each hello interval.
EIGRP sends its full routing table every 30 seconds.
questions.explanation: EIGRP only sends updates if a route has changed. Updates happen only after two routers have become neighbors and originally send their full route database and converge. If changes have not occurred, then the neighbor believes the route is still valid, under the condition that they are still neighbors.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which table is a router added to when it acknowledges a hello packet for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: When a router acknowledges a hello packet from a neighboring router, the router is added to the neighbor table of the router that sent the hello packet.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which is a condition that must be met for a router to become a neighbor router for EIGRP?
choices: Both routers have the same hello/hold interval.
Both routers are on the same subnet.
Both routers have the same link types.
Both routers have the same area ID.
questions.explanation: Although two routers can have different hello/hold intervals, they could still become neighbors. However, to do so they must be on the same subnet.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the definition of the reported distance for EIGRP?
choices: The remote router’s calculated metric for the remote network
The remote router’s calculated metric for the local network
The local router’s calculated metric for the remote network
The local router’s calculated metric for the local network
questions.explanation: The reported distance is the remote router’s calculated metric for the remote network. EIGRP uses this reported distance in its calculation for a feasible successor route.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which route will be entered into the routing table from EIGRP calculation of metrics?
questions.explanation: After DUAL calculates the metrics of the topology table, a successor route is calculated using the feasible distance. This route is populated into the routing table. A feasible successor route is also calculated based upon the reported distance and feasible distance.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which table does EIGRP use to calculate the feasible distance of a remote route?
questions.explanation: The topology table is used to calculate the feasible distance of a remote network. The DUAL routing algorithm interacts with the topology table to calculate this metric.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will create a routing process for EIGRP using an autonomous system number (ASN) of 20?
questions.explanation: The command to configure EIGRP with an ASN of 20 is router eigrp 20 .
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the default variance of EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The default variance is a value of 1 by default. This is because the variance is a multiplier that is applied to the feasible distance. All EIGRP routers multiply the feasible distance by 1 by default.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will change the router ID of an EIGRP router?
questions.explanation: The command eigrp router-id 2.2.2.2 configured in the sub- command of the router process will change the router ID to 2.2.2.2.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command should be used when configuring networks with discontiguous IP addresses for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The command no auto-summary will stop the router process of EIGRP from auto-summarizing network addresses. In a discontiguous network, this is problematic and should be turned off.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will advertise the network 192.168.1.0/24 for an EIGRP ASN of 20?
questions.explanation: The command network 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 will advertise the network of 192.168.1.0/24 for EIGRP with an ASN of 20. The .0.0.255 is a wildcard mask and matches bits in the last octet of the IP address.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You need to verify the adjacent routers participating in EIGRP. Which command will allow you to see the adjacent routers?
questions.explanation: The command show ip eigrp neighbors will allow you to inspect the routers that have created an adjacency with the current router you are working on.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to inspect the K metrics for EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The command show ip protocols will allow you to see specifics about the configured routing protocols. In the details of the output will be the K metrics for EIGRP.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You need to suppress EIGRP hello advertisements on the interface connecting you to your ISP. Which command will suppress EIGRP hello packets?
questions.explanation: The command passive-interface serial 0/0 configured inside the router process for EIGRP will set the Serial 0/0 as a passive interface. This will suppress EIGRP hello packets exiting the interface.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You want to confirm a Feasible-Successor route for EIGRP. Which command will allow you to verify this?
questions.explanation: The command show ip eigrp topology will allow you to see the calculated metrics for routes inside of the EIGRP topology table. For each network, the number of successors will be displayed. This information will help verify a feasible successor for a particular network.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You have two paths you want to load-balance that have slightly different delays. Which command will allow you to tune the unequal paths so they will load-balance with EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The variance command is configured in the router instance of EIGRP. The command variance 2 configures the router variance with a multiplier of 2.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: When is the command no passive-interface serial 0/0 used with EIGRP?
choices: When you want to allow hello packets exiting on interface serial 0/0
When you want to suppress hello packets from entering interface serial 0/0
When you want to allow hello packets to enter interface serial 0/0
When you want to suppress hello packets exiting on interface serial 0/0
questions.explanation: The command no passive-interface serial 0/0 is used when either passive-interface serial 0/0 or passive-interface default has been used in the router instance.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which mechanism in EIGRP allows for EIGRP to support multiple protocols?
questions.explanation: The protocol-dependent module (PDM) allows for multiple protocols to be supported with EIGRP. This allows for the same algorithm and methodology to be applied and for PDM-compliant modules such as IPv6, IP, and IPX to be used.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Two routers, Router A and Router B, will not form an adjacency with EIGRP. You discover that someone configured a custom K metric. Which command will configure the router’s K metrics back to their default setting?
questions.explanation: The command to configure the K metrics back to their default setting is no metric weights . This command should be entered in the router instance. The default metrics are K1=1, K2=0, K3=1, K4=0, K5=0.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the routes advertised by EIGRP?
questions.explanation: The command show ip protocols will display the networks that are being advertised on the current router.
questions.topic: 3.11 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the IPv6 address for EIGRPv6 neighbor discovery?
questions.explanation: The multicast address for neighbor discovery for EIGRPv6 is ff02::a.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command must be entered before EIGRPv6 can be configured?
questions.explanation: The ipv6 unicast-routing command must be entered first to enable the IPv6 protocol stack for routing.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command must be entered to start the EIGRPv6 router instance?
questions.explanation: The command no shutdown must be entered in the router instance to start EIGRPv6. By default, it is shut down.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You have configured EIGRPv6 with an ASN of 10. Which command will add networks to be advertised?
questions.explanation: When configuring EIGRPv6 to avoid erroneous duplication of IPv6 addresses, the interface is added to the EIGRPv6 routing process. This advertises all networks that are configured on the interface.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: When configuring a router with EIGRPv6 and only IPv6 is configured on the router, which command is necessary for EIGRPv6 operations?
questions.explanation: The command router-id 1.1.1.1 is required for EIGRPv6 operations. This command must be configured in the EIGRPv6 routing instance. The IPv4 address is the router’s ID, since EIGRPv6 requires an IPv4 router ID.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You have configured EIGRPv6 on a router that also faces your Internet service provider. Which command should you use to restrict hello packets from being directed to the ISP?
questions.explanation: The command to restrict hello packets from exiting the serial 0/0 interface is passive-interface serial 0/0 entered in the EIGRPv6 router instance.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You want to verify the K metrics that EIGRPv6 is using. Which command will display the K metrics?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 protocols will display the routing protocols running with IPv6. In the output of the EIGRPv6 instance, the K metrics will be displayed. Although show running-configuration will display the configured K-metrics, it will not show the default configuration.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will help you verify that a router has created an adjacency with EIGRPv6?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 eigrp neighbors will display the adjacencies the router has made with other EIGRPv6 routers.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will show only the EIGRPv6 routes?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 route eigrp will display only the EIGRPv6 routes.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You need to verify the interfaces that are participating in EIGRPv6. Which command will show this?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 protocols will display the routing protocols for IPv6. Included in this output are the interfaces participating in EIGRPv6.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which command will change the hello timer for EIGRPv6 ASN from 10 to 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: The command ipv6 hello-interval eigrp 10 5 will change the hello timer. It must be entered in the interface on which you want to change the hello interval.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: Which statement is true for EIGRP but not for EIGRPv6?
choices: K metrics must match for an adjacency to form.
Hello and holddown timers must match for an adjacency to form.
Interfaces must be on the same subnet for an adjacency to form.
questions.explanation: Interfaces for EIGRP must be on the same subnet for an adjacency to form. However, that is not a requirement for EIGRPv6.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: You need to calculate a variance for EIGRPv6. Which table will allow you to calculate the variance for unequal-cost load balancing?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 eigrp topology will allow you to verify the metrics. From this, you can calculate the variance multiplier for unequal-cost load balancing.
questions.topic: 3.12 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot EIGRP for IPv6 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution, stub)

questions.question: What is the maximum hop count for RIP?
questions.explanation: The maximum hop count for RIP is 15. A hop count over 15 hops is considered unroutable or unreachable.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which statement is true about RIPv2 advertisements?
choices: RIPv2 allows for neighborship through hello packets.
RIPv2 multicasts the full routing table every 60 seconds.
RIPv2 multicasts the full routing table every 30 seconds.
RIPv2 broadcasts only updates on all active interfaces.
questions.explanation: By default, RIPv2 multicasts the full routing table on all active interfaces every 30 seconds.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which metric does RIPv2 use to calculate routes?
questions.explanation: RIPv2 uses hop count to calculate routes. When a router sends its routing table, the next router adds a +1 to the metric for the entries in the table.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which multicast address does RIPv2 use for advertising routes?
questions.explanation: RIPv2 uses the multicast address of 224.0.0.9 to advertise routes.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: When RIP is configured on a router, what must be configured to allow for classless routing?
questions.explanation: When you’re configuring RIP on a router, the RIP process will default to RIPv1, which is classful. The command version 2 must be configured in the router instance of RIP to allow for RIPv2.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: You need to configure the advertisement of the network 192.168.1.0/24 for RIPv2. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command network 192.168.1.0 will configure the RIPv2 route process to advertise the network 192.168.1.0.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see the next advertisement interval for RIPv2?
questions.explanation: The command show ip protocols will display the next interval when RIPv2 advertisements are sent out.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to inspect RIPv2 calculations for routes discovered?
questions.explanation: The command show ip rip database will display all of the discovered routes and their calculated metrics.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: You have RIPv2 configured on an Internet-facing router. Which command will propagate the default route to all other RIPv2 routers?
questions.explanation: The command default-information originate will advertise the default route to all other RIPv2 routers.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to inspect RIPv2 advertisements?
questions.explanation: The command debug ip rip will allow you to see advertisements in real time.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: You need to advertise the routes of 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24, and 192.168.3.0/24. Which configuration will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The three Class C networks need to be advertised separately. RIPv2 uses the default class network mask when configuring networks.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: You have RIPv2 configured on an Internet-facing router. Which command will suppress RIPv2 advertisements on the interface link?
questions.explanation: The command passive-interface serial 0/0 configured in the router instance will suppress updates from exiting interface Serial 0/0.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: What is the default invalid timer for RIPv2?
questions.explanation: The default invalid timer for RIP is 180 seconds. This holddown timer is six times the advertisement interval of 30 seconds.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which is a problem with using RIPv2 in a network?
questions.explanation: RIPv2 has extremely slow convergence time. This is because the advertisement of routes is every 30 seconds. So a router four hops away potentially could take 120 seconds before discovering the route.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which technique is used to stop routing loops with RIPv2?
questions.explanation: Split horizons are used to stop routing loops with RIPv2. Split horizons prevent a router from advertising a route to a router in which the original route was discovered.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which algorithm does RIPv2 use to calculate routes?
questions.explanation: RIPv2 uses the Bellman-Ford algorithm to calculate its metrics.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will need to be configured for support of discontinuous networks?
questions.explanation: The command no auto-summary will stop the router process of RIPv2 from auto-summarizing network addresses. In a discontiguous network, this is problematic and should be turned off.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command configures RIPv2 on a router and advertises a network of 192.168.20.0/24?
questions.explanation: Configuring RIPv2 begins with configuration of the router instance of RIP via the command router rip . RIPv2 is configured inside of the router instance with the command version 2 . Then the network of 192.168.20.0/24 is advertised with the command network 192.168.20.0 .
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the RIPv2 holddown timer?
choices: Holddown timers allow for time between when a route becomes invalid and it is flushed from the routing table.
Holddown timers allow for time between when a route has become unreachable and when it can be updated again.
Holddown timers define the time when a route becomes invalid.
Holddown timers define the time when a valid route is present in the routing table.
questions.explanation: The holddown timer’s job is to allow the network to stabilize after a route had become unreachable via an update. This limits the potential problems related to a flapping port and allows RIPv2 to converge route updates in the entire network.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: What is the default number of equal-cost routes RIPv2 will load balance?
questions.explanation: The default number of routes that RIPv2 will load balance is a total of 4.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which protocol will support IPv6 for RIP?
questions.explanation: RIPng is the next generation of the RIP protocol for use with IPv6.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will display which routes the RIPv2 router is advertising?
questions.explanation: The command show ip rip database will display the routes being advertised by RIPv2. These routes will be identified with the directly connected statement.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: How would you configure a router to use split horizons for RIPv2?
questions.explanation: The command ip spilt-horizon configured on the interface will configure split-horizon processing for RIPv2.
questions.topic: 3.13 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot RIPv2 for IPv4 (excluding authentication, filtering, manual summarization, redistribution)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to check basic connectivity at layer 3?
questions.explanation: The ping command will allow basic connectivity testing at layer 3.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see the path on which a packet gets routed to its destination?
questions.explanation: The command traceroute will allow you to verify the path on which a packet gets routed.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: You perform a ping to a host on the network. However, the first packet is dropped. Why did the first packet drop?
choices: The remote router dropped the first packet.
The ARP request timed out the ping packet.
The local router dropped the first packet.
questions.explanation: The ARP request took time for the ARP reply, and during this time, the ICMP timeout threshold was exceeded. This is common on a router, and the following pings should not time out unless the ARP entry is cleared after its TTL expires.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: Which command on Windows will allow you to verify your IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and MAC address?
questions.explanation: The command ipconfig /all will help you verify the IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and MAC address of your computer. The command of ipconfig doesn’t show the MAC address.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: Which command on Windows will allow you to verify the path a packet gets routed through on the network?
questions.explanation: The Windows command for tracing a route is tracert .
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: You ping from a router to another router and receive back !!!!! . What does this mean?
choices: There is congestion in the path.
The packets were received, but after the ICMP timeout.
questions.explanation: When you see an exclamation mark, it means that the packets were successfully acknowledged on the other side and an ICMP response was received.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: You want to ping a router on your network from interface Serial 0/0 and not the path in the routing table. How can you achieve this?
choices: Configure a temporary route for the router exiting the interface.
This cannot be done; packets cannot disregard the routing table.
Enter the interface in configuration mode, and ping the remote router.
Enter extended ping, and specify the exit interface.
questions.explanation: The extended ping command allows you to specify a number of parameters such as repeat count, datagram size, and source address or exit interface. There are several other parameters that can be adjusted.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: You perform a traceroute to a destination network and receive back several lines of output. On the end of each line are three parameters such as 1 192.168.1.1 20 msec 34 msec 67 msec . What do they mean?
choices: They are the minimum, average, and maximum of the ICMP query.
They are the maximum, average, and minimum of the ICMP query.
They are the three response times of each ICMP request.
They are the minimum, maximum, and average of the ICMP query.
questions.explanation: The three times are the minimum response time, average response time, and maximum response time of the ICMP Echo and Reply.
questions.topic: 3.14 Troubleshoot basic Layer 3 end-to-end connectivity issues

questions.question: You need to make a Telnet connection to a remote router from a router you are configuring. Which command will allow you to do this?
questions.explanation: The IP address or hostname entered in privileged exec mode will create a direct Telnet request. Alternatively, you can specify the command telnet 198.56.33.3 .

questions.question: An administrator calls you and states that they believe an interface is down on a router you maintain. Which command will show only the interface, the IP address configured, and the status of the interface?
questions.explanation: The command show ip interface brief will display only the necessary information of interface, IP, and status to aid in the diagnostic process.

questions.question: You need to ping an IPv6 address of 2001:db8:3:4::2. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The normal ping command will achieve this task. Originally in Windows XP, the command ping6 was used in lieu of the command ping . The command ping6 is also found in Linux. However, today, most operating systems have extended the ping command to both IPv4 and IPv6.

questions.question: Which IPv6 command will verify that you have received a Router Advertisement message from a local router?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 neighbors will display all of the neighboring routers that have sent a Router Advertisement message. This cache will normally contain the link-local addresses of the neighboring routers.
